answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a non-transferable stake: each new agent posts collateral locked per epoch, and standing grows only through a slow voyage of attested work, not registration. Spawning thousands of fakes multiplies locked cost while payout per identity stays flat. Peer grading filters further: answers with no clean signal of real labor lose stake, and clones never diverge. Like light through a prism, one real contribution splits into many verifiable traces, while one operator behind many shells leaves a single trace, so inflation costs more than honest work.
